questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The first newspaper published in India was:
questions.explanation: The Bengal Gazette, started by James Augustus Hickey in January 1780, was the first newspaper printed in India. The Times of India is wrong — it was established in 1838. The Hindu is wrong — it was founded in 1878. Bombay Samachar is wrong — it was founded in 1822 (though it's the oldest surviving newspaper).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Indian newspapers:

(i) 'Kesari' was started by Bal Gangadhar Tilak in Marathi.
(ii) 'Young India' was a journal edited by Mahatma Gandhi.
(iii) 'The Statesman' is published from Mumbai.
(iv) 'Bombay Samachar' is the oldest surviving newspaper in Asia.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Tilak started 'Kesari' (a Marathi-language newspaper) in 1881 along with 'Maratha' (in English). (ii) is correct — 'Young India' was a weekly journal edited by Gandhi from 1919 to propagate his ideas of non-violence. (iv) is correct — Bombay Samachar (founded 1822 in Gujarati) is the oldest continuously published newspaper in Asia. (iii) is wrong — The Statesman is published from Kolkata (and Delhi), not Mumbai.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who is the author of the book 'Discovery of India'?
questions.explanation: 'The Discovery of India' was written by Jawaharlal Nehru during his imprisonment at Ahmednagar Fort (1942–1946). Mahatma Gandhi is wrong — he wrote 'My Experiments with Truth'. Rabindranath Tagore is wrong — he wrote 'Gitanjali'. S. Radhakrishnan is wrong — he wrote 'Indian Philosophy'.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Bal Gangadhar Tilak used newspapers as a powerful tool for the freedom movement.
Reason (R): Through 'Kesari' (Marathi) and 'Maratha' (English), Tilak awakened nationalist consciousness and was prosecuted multiple times for sedition.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Tilak effectively used journalism for the freedom struggle. Reason (R) is also correct — Kesari and Maratha were vehicles for his nationalist ideology, leading to sedition charges. (R) explains (A) by providing specific examples of how he used newspapers. Option 2 is wrong because (R) directly supports (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following newspapers/journals with their founders:

Column I:
(a) Bengal Gazette
(b) Sambad Kaumudi
(c) Harijan
(d) Yugantar

Column II:
(i) Mahatma Gandhi
(ii) James Augustus Hickey
(iii) Barindra Kumar Ghosh and Bhupendranath Dutta
(iv) Raja Ram Mohan Roy

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Bengal Gazette was started by James Augustus Hickey (1780) — matches (ii). (b) Sambad Kaumudi was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy (1821) — matches (iv). (c) Harijan was published by Mahatma Gandhi (1933) — matches (i). (d) Yugantar was a revolutionary newspaper associated with Barindra Kumar Ghosh — matches (iii). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following books were written by Mahatma Gandhi?

(i) My Experiments with Truth (autobiography)
(ii) Hind Swaraj
(iii) India Wins Freedom
(iv) The Story of My Deportation

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — 'My Experiments with Truth' is Gandhi's autobiography. (ii) is correct — 'Hind Swaraj' (Indian Home Rule, 1909) was written by Gandhi on his views on self-governance. (iii) is wrong — 'India Wins Freedom' was written by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad. (iv) is wrong — 'The Story of My Deportation' was written by Lala Lajpat Rai.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The newspaper 'The Hindu' is published from which city?
questions.explanation: The Hindu was founded in 1878 in Madras (now Chennai) and its headquarters remain there. 'Delhi' is wrong — while it has a Delhi edition, the headquarters are in Chennai. 'Mumbai' is wrong — The Times of India is headquartered in Mumbai. 'Kolkata' is wrong — The Statesman is based in Kolkata.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about 'Gitanjali':

(i) It was written by Rabindranath Tagore.
(ii) It won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.
(iii) It is a collection of poems originally written in Bengali.
(iv) It was first published in Hindi.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Tagore wrote Gitanjali (Song Offerings). (ii) is correct — the English translation of Gitanjali won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913. (iii) is correct — it was originally composed in Bengali, then translated to English by Tagore himself. (iv) is wrong — it was originally written in BENGALI, not Hindi.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The book 'Wings of Fire' is the autobiography of __________.
questions.explanation: 'Wings of Fire' (1999) is the autobiography of Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, describing his journey from humble beginnings to leading India's missile programme. Jawaharlal Nehru is wrong — his autobiography is 'Toward Freedom'. Indira Gandhi is wrong — she did not write an autobiography by this name. Sardar Patel is wrong — he is not associated with this book.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Raja Ram Mohan Roy is called the 'Father of Indian Journalism'.
Reason (R): He started several newspapers including 'Sambad Kaumudi' (Bengali, 1821) and 'Mirat-ul-Akhbar' (Persian, 1822) and fought for press freedom.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Ram Mohan Roy is honoured as the Father of Indian Journalism. Reason (R) is also correct — he founded influential newspapers and petitioned against press restrictions. (R) explains (A) because his pioneering journalistic work is exactly why he earned this title. Option 2 is wrong because (R) gives the specific justification. Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which newspaper was started by Motilal Nehru?
questions.explanation: Motilal Nehru started 'The Independent' newspaper in 1919 from Lucknow to support the nationalist cause. 'The Pioneer' is wrong — it was a British-owned paper. 'The Statesman' is wrong — it was established by the British. 'The Tribune' is wrong — it was founded by Sardar Dyal Singh Majithia in 1881.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following authors with their books:

Column I:
(a) R.K. Narayan
(b) Mulk Raj Anand
(c) Vikram Seth
(d) Arundhati Roy

Column II:
(i) The God of Small Things
(ii) A Suitable Boy
(iii) Malgudi Days
(iv) Untouchable

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) R.K. Narayan wrote 'Malgudi Days' — matches (iii). (b) Mulk Raj Anand wrote 'Untouchable' (1935) — matches (iv). (c) Vikram Seth wrote 'A Suitable Boy' — matches (ii). (d) Arundhati Roy wrote 'The God of Small Things' (Booker Prize 1997) — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was significant because:
options: It restricted the freedom of Indian-language newspapers to criticise British policies
It promoted the growth of Indian newspapers
It established English as the only newspaper language
It provided government funding to newspapers
questions.correctAnswer: It restricted the freedom of Indian-language newspapers to criticise British policies
questions.explanation: The Vernacular Press Act (1878) under Lord Lytton imposed restrictions on Indian-language newspapers, empowering the government to confiscate presses printing 'seditious' material. 'Promoted growth' is wrong — it suppressed, not promoted, the press. 'Established English as only language' is wrong — it targeted vernacular press, not mandated English. 'Provided funding' is wrong — it imposed restrictions, not support.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Indian authors and Nobel Prizes:

(i) Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature (1913).
(ii) V.S. Naipaul won the Nobel Prize in Literature (2001).
(iii) Salman Rushdie won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
(iv) Amartya Sen won the Nobel Prize in Economics (1998).

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Tagore won the 1913 Nobel in Literature for Gitanjali. (ii) is correct — V.S. Naipaul (of Indian-Trinidadian origin) won the 2001 Nobel in Literature. (iv) is correct — Amartya Sen won the 1998 Nobel in Economics. (iii) is wrong — Salman Rushdie has NOT won the Nobel Prize in Literature (he won the Booker Prize for 'Midnight's Children').

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who founded 'The Times of India'?
options: It was founded as 'The Bombay Times and Journal of Commerce' in 1838
questions.correctAnswer: It was founded as 'The Bombay Times and Journal of Commerce' in 1838
questions.explanation: The Times of India was originally established as 'The Bombay Times and Journal of Commerce' in 1838, making it one of India's oldest English newspapers. 'Nehru in 1947' is wrong — it predates independence by over a century. 'Gandhi in 1920' is wrong — Gandhi's journal was 'Young India'. 'Lord Curzon in 1905' is wrong — he was a Viceroy, not a newspaper founder.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 'Hind Swaraj' is considered one of the most important books in India's freedom struggle.
Reason (R): Written by Gandhi in 1909, it presents his vision of Indian self-rule through non-violence, rejecting Western materialism and industrialisation.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Hind Swaraj is a foundational text of India's independence philosophy. Reason (R) is also correct — Gandhi wrote it on a ship in 1909, outlining his vision of Swaraj through non-violence. (R) explains (A) because the content described in (R) is what made the book so influential. Option 2 is wrong because (R) explains why it's important. Option 3 is wrong because (R) is accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly matched (newspaper — language)?

(i) Dainik Jagran — Hindi
(ii) Anandabazar Patrika — Bengali
(iii) Eenadu — Tamil
(iv) Punjab Kesari — Hindi/Punjabi

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Dainik Jagran is India's most-read Hindi daily. (ii) is correct — Anandabazar Patrika is a leading Bengali daily from Kolkata. (iv) is correct — Punjab Kesari is published in Hindi (with editions in Punjabi). (iii) is wrong — Eenadu is published in TELUGU, not Tamil. Tamil dailies include Dinamalar and Dinathanthi.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The book 'Arthashastra' was written by:
questions.explanation: The Arthashastra, an ancient treatise on statecraft, economics, and military strategy, was written by Kautilya (also called Chanakya/Vishnugupta), the advisor to Chandragupta Maurya. Kalidasa is wrong — he was a playwright/poet (Shakuntala, Meghaduta). Valmiki is wrong — he wrote the Ramayana. Aryabhata is wrong — he wrote mathematical/astronomical treatises.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following newspapers with their cities of publication:

Column I:
(a) The Hindu
(b) The Statesman
(c) The Tribune
(d) Deccan Herald

Column II:
(i) Bengaluru
(ii) Kolkata
(iii) Chandigarh
(iv) Chennai

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) The Hindu — Chennai (Madras) — matches (iv). (b) The Statesman — Kolkata (and Delhi) — matches (ii). (c) The Tribune — Chandigarh (founded in Lahore, moved after partition) — matches (iii). (d) Deccan Herald — Bengaluru (Karnataka) — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Premchand:

(i) He is considered the greatest Hindi novelist and short story writer.
(ii) His famous works include 'Godan', 'Gaban', and 'Nirmala'.
(iii) He wrote exclusively in English.
(iv) He is called the 'Upanyas Samrat' (Emperor of Novels).

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Premchand (1880–1936) is the greatest figure in Hindi/Urdu literature. (ii) is correct — Godan, Gaban, and Nirmala are his masterpieces. (iv) is correct — he is called 'Upanyas Samrat' for his numerous influential novels. (iii) is wrong — Premchand wrote in HINDI and URDU, not English.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The oldest surviving newspaper in India is:
questions.explanation: Bombay Samachar (founded 1822 in Gujarati) is the oldest newspaper still in continuous publication in India and Asia. 'Bengal Gazette' is wrong — though it was the FIRST newspaper (1780), it ceased publication in 1782 and doesn't survive. 'The Times of India' is wrong — founded 1838, younger than Bombay Samachar. 'The Hindu' is wrong — founded 1878, much younger.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The book 'India Wins Freedom' was written by __________.
questions.explanation: 'India Wins Freedom' (1959) is Maulana Abul Kalam Azad's account of India's independence and partition. Jawaharlal Nehru is wrong — he wrote 'The Discovery of India'. Sardar Patel is wrong — he is not associated with this book. Mahatma Gandhi is wrong — he wrote 'My Experiments with Truth'.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Arundhati Roy's 'The God of Small Things' is internationally acclaimed.
Reason (R): It won the Man Booker Prize in 1997, making Roy the first Indian to receive this prestigious literary award.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — the novel is internationally celebrated. Reason (R) is also correct — it won the 1997 Booker Prize, making Roy the first Indian citizen to win it. (R) explains (A) because winning the Booker Prize is what gave the book its international acclaim. Option 2 is wrong because (R) directly explains (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following journals/newspapers were edited by Mahatma Gandhi?

(i) Young India
(ii) Harijan
(iii) Indian Opinion
(iv) Kesari

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Gandhi edited 'Young India' (1919–1932), a weekly English journal. (ii) is correct — Gandhi started 'Harijan' (1933) focusing on the upliftment of untouchables. (iii) is correct — 'Indian Opinion' was started by Gandhi in South Africa (1903). (iv) is wrong — 'Kesari' was started and edited by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, not Gandhi.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The epic poem 'Ramayana' was written by:
questions.explanation: The original Sanskrit epic Ramayana was composed by Maharishi Valmiki. Vyasa is wrong — he authored the Mahabharata. Tulsidas is wrong — he wrote 'Ramcharitmanas' (a retelling in Awadhi Hindi), not the original Ramayana. Kalidasa is wrong — he wrote plays like Abhijnanasakuntalam.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following books with their authors:

Column I:
(a) Midnight's Children
(b) A Passage to India
(c) Kim
(d) The White Tiger

Column II:
(i) Rudyard Kipling
(ii) Salman Rushdie
(iii) Aravind Adiga
(iv) E.M. Forster

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Midnight's Children — Salman Rushdie (Booker of Bookers) — matches (ii). (b) A Passage to India — E.M. Forster — matches (iv). (c) Kim — Rudyard Kipling (Nobel 1907) — matches (i). (d) The White Tiger — Aravind Adiga (Booker 2008) — matches (iii). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about 'The Tribune' newspaper:

(i) It was founded by Sardar Dyal Singh Majithia in 1881.
(ii) It was originally published from Lahore.
(iii) After partition, it moved to Chandigarh.
(iv) It is published in Tamil.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Sardar Dyal Singh Majithia founded The Tribune in 1881. (ii) is correct — it was originally published from Lahore. (iii) is correct — after the 1947 partition (Lahore went to Pakistan), it relocated to Simla and then Chandigarh. (iv) is wrong — The Tribune is published in ENGLISH (and Hindi edition 'Dainik Tribune'), not Tamil.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who wrote 'Panchatantra'?
questions.explanation: The Panchatantra, a collection of animal fables teaching niti (wise conduct), was composed by Vishnu Sharma (circa 3rd century BC). Kalidas is wrong — he wrote plays and poetry. Chanakya is wrong — he wrote Arthashastra. Bhasa is wrong — he was an ancient dramatist (Swapnavasavadatta).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was repealed in 1882.
Reason (R): Lord Ripon, a liberal Viceroy, repealed the Act believing in press freedom and Indian rights.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — the Vernacular Press Act was repealed in 1882. Reason (R) is also correct — Lord Ripon (Viceroy 1880–84) was a liberal reformer who believed the Act was unjust. (R) explains (A) because Ripon's liberal views directly led to the repeal. Option 2 is wrong because (R) gives the reason for (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are major English-language dailies of India?

(i) The Times of India
(ii) Hindustan Times
(iii) Dainik Bhaskar
(iv) The Indian Express

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) The Times of India — English daily ✓. (ii) Hindustan Times — English daily ✓. (iv) The Indian Express — English daily ✓. (iii) Dainik Bhaskar is wrong — it is a HINDI daily (Dainik = daily in Hindi), not English.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The author of 'Meghaduta' (Cloud Messenger) is:
questions.explanation: Meghaduta is a lyric poem by Kalidasa (c. 4th–5th century) about a yaksha sending a message to his beloved through a cloud. Tulsidas is wrong — he wrote Ramcharitmanas. Surdas is wrong — he was a devotional poet of Krishna. Kabir is wrong — he was a mystic poet of the Bhakti movement.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about 'Navjivan':

(i) It was a Gujarati-language journal.
(ii) It was published by Mahatma Gandhi.
(iii) It was started during British rule to spread nationalist ideas.
(iv) It was India's first English-language newspaper.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Navjivan was a Gujarati journal (also had a Hindi version). (ii) is correct — Gandhi published Navjivan from 1919 to spread his message. (iii) is correct — it was started during British rule for nationalist propaganda. (iv) is wrong — Navjivan was in GUJARATI/Hindi, not English; the first English newspaper was Bengal Gazette.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following classic Indian texts with their subjects:

Column I:
(a) Arthashastra
(b) Kamasutra
(c) Natyashastra
(d) Charaka Samhita

Column II:
(i) Medicine (Ayurveda)
(ii) Statecraft and economics
(iii) Performing arts (drama, dance, music)
(iv) Human relationships and behaviour

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Arthashastra by Kautilya — statecraft/economics — matches (ii). (b) Kamasutra by Vatsyayana — human relationships — matches (iv). (c) Natyashastra by Bharata Muni — drama/performing arts — matches (iii). (d) Charaka Samhita — ancient Ayurvedic medical text — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who is the author of 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth'?
questions.explanation: 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth' (Satya na Prayogo) is Gandhi's autobiography, originally written in Gujarati (1927–29). Jawaharlal Nehru is wrong — his autobiography is 'Toward Freedom'/'An Autobiography'. B.R. Ambedkar is wrong — he wrote 'Annihilation of Caste'. Subhas Chandra Bose is wrong — he wrote 'The Indian Struggle'.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Indian literary awards:

(i) The Sahitya Akademi Award is given for outstanding literary work in Indian languages.
(ii) The Jnanpith Award is India's highest literary honour.
(iii) The first Jnanpith Award was given in 1965.
(iv) The Sahitya Akademi was established by the United Nations.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Sahitya Akademi Awards recognise outstanding literary works in 24 Indian languages. (ii) is correct — the Jnanpith Award (instituted by Bharatiya Jnanpith trust) is the highest Indian literary award. (iii) is correct — the first Jnanpith Award was given in 1965 to G. Sankara Kurup (Malayalam). (iv) is wrong — the Sahitya Akademi was established by the GOVERNMENT OF INDIA in 1954, not the UN.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The newspaper 'Amrita Bazar Patrika' was originally published in:
questions.explanation: Amrita Bazar Patrika was originally a Bengali newspaper, but after the Vernacular Press Act (1878), it overnight converted to English to escape the Act's restrictions on Indian-language papers. 'English only' is wrong — it started in Bengali. 'Hindi only' is wrong — it was a Bengali paper. 'Urdu only' is wrong — it was not an Urdu paper.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Premchand's novel 'Godan' is considered a masterpiece of Hindi literature.
Reason (R): 'Godan' realistically portrays the struggles of Indian peasants under zamindari exploitation and debt, making it socially relevant and artistically powerful.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Godan (1936) is universally regarded as a Hindi literary masterpiece. Reason (R) is also correct — it depicts the tragic life of the peasant Hori under landlord oppression and debt. (R) explains (A) because its realistic portrayal and social relevance are what make it a masterpiece. Option 2 is wrong because (R) provides the reasons. Option 3 is wrong because (R) is accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who wrote the national song 'Vande Mataram'?
questions.explanation: 'Vande Mataram' was composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in his novel 'Anandamath' (1882). It was adopted as India's National Song. Rabindranath Tagore is wrong — he composed the National Anthem 'Jana Gana Mana'. Muhammad Iqbal is wrong — he wrote 'Saare Jahan Se Accha'. Sarojini Naidu is wrong — she was a poet but didn't write Vande Mataram.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following freedom-era journals with their editors:

Column I:
(a) Commonweal
(b) New India
(c) Pradhan
(d) Al-Hilal

Column II:
(i) Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
(ii) Annie Besant
(iii) Annie Besant
(iv) Ganesh Shankar Vidyarthi

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Commonweal was edited by Annie Besant — matches (ii). (b) New India was also edited by Annie Besant — matches (iii). (c) Pratap/Pradhan was edited by Ganesh Shankar Vidyarthi — matches (iv). (d) Al-Hilal (Urdu weekly) was edited by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (a) and (d).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Hindi-language newspapers?

(i) Dainik Jagran
(ii) Amar Ujala
(iii) Malayala Manorama
(iv) Hindustan (Hindi daily)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) Dainik Jagran — Hindi daily (most-read in India) ✓. (ii) Amar Ujala — Hindi daily ✓. (iv) Hindustan — Hindi daily published by HT Media ✓. (iii) Malayala Manorama is wrong — it is published in MALAYALAM (Kerala's language), not Hindi.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The book 'Annihilation of Caste' was written by:
questions.explanation: 'Annihilation of Caste' (1936) is a landmark work by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar that critiques the Hindu caste system and calls for its destruction. Mahatma Gandhi is wrong — he wrote about caste reform but not this specific work. Nehru is wrong — he wrote political works. E.V. Ramasamy Periyar is wrong — while he fought against caste, this book is Ambedkar's.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Booker Prize and Indian authors:

(i) Salman Rushdie won the Booker Prize for 'Midnight's Children' (1981).
(ii) Kiran Desai won the Booker Prize for 'The Inheritance of Loss' (2006).
(iii) Aravind Adiga won the Booker Prize for 'The White Tiger' (2008).
(iv) R.K. Narayan won the Booker Prize for 'Malgudi Days'.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Rushdie won the Booker in 1981 for Midnight's Children. (ii) is correct — Kiran Desai won in 2006 for The Inheritance of Loss. (iii) is correct — Aravind Adiga won in 2008 for The White Tiger. (iv) is wrong — R.K. Narayan was nominated but NEVER won the Booker Prize.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Press Council of India' was established to:
options: Preserve the freedom of the press and maintain standards of journalism
Provide financial aid to newspaper owners
questions.correctAnswer: Preserve the freedom of the press and maintain standards of journalism
questions.explanation: The Press Council of India (established 1966) is a statutory body that safeguards press freedom while ensuring responsible journalism. 'Censor newspapers' is wrong — it doesn't censor; it is a self-regulatory body. 'Publish government newspapers' is wrong — it's a regulatory body, not a publisher. 'Financial aid to owners' is wrong — it doesn't provide financial assistance.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following autobiographies with their authors:

Column I:
(a) My Experiments with Truth
(b) Wings of Fire
(c) An Autobiography (Toward Freedom)
(d) The Indian Struggle

Column II:
(i) Subhas Chandra Bose
(ii) Mahatma Gandhi
(iii) Jawaharlal Nehru
(iv) A.P.J. Abdul Kalam

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) My Experiments with Truth — Gandhi — matches (ii). (b) Wings of Fire — Kalam — matches (iv). (c) An Autobiography / Toward Freedom — Nehru — matches (iii). (d) The Indian Struggle — Subhas Chandra Bose — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who composed the Indian National Anthem 'Jana Gana Mana'?
questions.explanation: The National Anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' was composed by Rabindranath Tagore in Bengali (1911) and adopted as India's anthem on 24 January 1950. Bankim Chandra is wrong — he wrote 'Vande Mataram' (National Song). Sarojini Naidu is wrong — she was a poet but didn't compose the anthem. Muhammad Iqbal is wrong — he wrote 'Saare Jahan Se Accha'.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about news agencies in India:

(i) PTI (Press Trust of India) is India's largest news agency.
(ii) UNI (United News of India) is another major Indian news agency.
(iii) Reuters is an Indian news agency.
(iv) ANI (Asian News International) is a multimedia news agency.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — PTI (founded 1947) is India's premier and largest news agency. (ii) is correct — UNI (founded 1961) is another major Indian news agency. (iv) is correct — ANI is a prominent Indian multimedia news agency providing video content. (iii) is wrong — Reuters is a BRITISH international news agency (founded in London, 1851), not Indian.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The book 'Glimpses of World History' was written by:
questions.explanation: 'Glimpses of World History' (1934) was written by Jawaharlal Nehru as a series of letters to his daughter Indira while in prison, covering world history from ancient civilizations to modern times. Gandhi is wrong — he wrote philosophical/autobiographical works. Tagore is wrong — he wrote poetry and fiction. Radhakrishnan is wrong — he wrote philosophical works on Indian thought.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following is NOT a work by Rabindranath Tagore?

(i) Gitanjali
(ii) Gora
(iii) Godan
(iv) The Post Office

Select the correct option:
questions.explanation: (iii) 'Godan' was written by PREMCHAND, not Tagore. (i) Gitanjali — Tagore ✓. (ii) Gora — Tagore ✓ (a novel). (iv) The Post Office (Dakghar) — Tagore ✓ (a play). Only Godan does not belong to Tagore.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Pulitzer Prize is awarded for excellence in __________.
options: Journalism, literature, and musical composition (in the United States)
questions.correctAnswer: Journalism, literature, and musical composition (in the United States)
questions.explanation: The Pulitzer Prize (established 1917, Columbia University) is awarded annually for distinguished American journalism, literature, and musical composition. 'Scientific research' is wrong — that's the Nobel Prize. 'Sports achievement' is wrong — that's the Arjuna/Khel Ratna awards. 'Architecture' is wrong — that's the Pritzker Prize.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about freedom-era newspapers:

(i) 'Swadeshimitran' was a Tamil newspaper that supported the nationalist movement.
(ii) 'Mathrubhumi' is a Malayalam newspaper founded during the freedom struggle era.
(iii) 'Sandesh' was a Gujarati newspaper associated with the freedom movement.
(iv) All Indian newspapers were in English during the freedom struggle.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Swadeshimitran (1882) was a Tamil nationalist newspaper from Madras. (ii) is correct — Mathrubhumi (1923) is a Malayalam newspaper that actively supported the independence movement. (iii) is correct — Sandesh (founded 1923 in Ahmedabad) is a Gujarati newspaper with freedom movement connections. (iv) is wrong — numerous newspapers were published in vernacular languages (Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Tamil, Urdu) — the freedom press was multilingual.
